items.title: 7.6 Ethical Issues in Data Science and Analysis

source_refs.note: Topic 7.6 with the Do You Know (PDF 101-102); no figure, and the bias examples are carried as a table. Short Q9-10, Long Q6 and MCQ 10 are answered here. The check question is added.

blocks.text: Ethical issues are a major concern in data science. As data is collected and analysed on a large scale, it must be handled responsibly: ethical practice keeps decisions fair, accurate and trusted, while poor standards can lead to misuse of data and harm to individuals or groups. Data scientists must follow ethical guidelines when collecting, processing and interpreting data, with transparency and accountability at every stage.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: Biased data can produce unfair results; ethical data science protects privacy, avoids discrimination and builds trust in technology.
Bias in data collection and analysis

Bias in data collection happens when the data does not fairly represent all groups, for example because of limited sources or unfair sampling; during analysis, personal assumptions can also add bias. Biased data gives inaccurate, misleading results that can reinforce unfair outcomes, so bias must be identified and reduced through careful collection and objective analysis.

blocks.caption: Examples of bias
rows: A survey on student performance is done only in top-performing schools, ignoring average and low-performing ones
A health study includes only young adults, so its results do not represent older people
A hiring dataset contains mostly male candidates, so a model trained on it favours male applicants
Data collected only in urban areas is used to make decisions for rural people
A researcher focuses only on data that supports their belief and ignores results that contradict it

blocks.text: Ethical use of data and models

items: Respect privacy and confidentiality; collect data only with proper consent and use it only for the stated purpose.
Design machine learning models to avoid discrimination.
Protect sensitive data from unauthorised access.
Follow ethical guidelines to prevent misuse of predictive models, and be transparent about how models work, which builds trust.

blocks.text: Results should be presented honestly, without exaggeration or manipulation; the limitations of the data and analysis must be stated clearly; and misleading visuals or selective reporting must be avoided. Clear, truthful explanation helps people understand results correctly, prevents misuse and strengthens trust in data analysis.

blocks.prompt: A face-recognition system is trained mostly on photos of light-skinned adults. What kind of bias is this, and what harm could it cause?
blocks.explanation: Sampling bias: the data does not represent all groups. The system may recognise darker-skinned people or children less accurately, leading to wrongful matches or denied access; the fix is more representative training data and testing for each group.

items: Handle data responsibly: fairness, accuracy, transparency, accountability.
Bias types: survey, sampling, gender, geographical, confirmation.
Ethical use: consent, privacy, no discrimination; report honestly with limitations.
